Hardware:

* Lenovo ThinkPad P50

* 7.3.4-200.fc44.x86_64

The amdkfd_query_rdma_interface is using the old EXPORT_SYMBOL instead of EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL.

```
/**

 *
 * \param interace     - OUT: Pointer to interface
 *

{
        *ops  = &rdma_ops;

}

issues.title: [DCN401] Cursor stutters on Xorg with two displays: static CRTC enables idle optimizations, so each cursor update does DMUB idle exit/enter
issues.author: Cláudio Forain
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

With **two displays active** on Xorg, the mouse cursor visibly speeds up and slows down while the desktop is otherwise idle. Physical mouse movement is steady, but on-screen motion is uneven. It reproduces every time and is easy to see.

* **Single display** (`xrandr --output DisplayPort-1 --off`): smooth.
* **Any rendering activity** (a tiny GL loop): smooth.
* **Kernels:** 7.1.12, 7.2.x and 7.3.3 are affected. 7.1.5 is not, because it still had [a1fc7bf6677e](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=a1fc7bf6677e) (“drm/amd/display: Restore 5s vbl offdelay for NV3x+ DGPUs”). That workaround was reverted by [f39283eab44f](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=f39283eab44f), which reached stable in 7.1.6. Older kernels (6.18.x) were also affected.
* Disabling GFXOFF, forcing `power_dpm_force_performance_level=high`, and `amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x800` (DC_DISABLE_IPS) do **not** help.

### Root cause (from ftrace + code reading)

Idle optimizations are HW-wide, but the ISM runs **per CRTC**. `dm_ism_commit_idle_optimization_state()` allows idle optimizations globally when `!vblank_enabled && dm->active_vblank_irq_count == 0`. It doesn’t check whether the **other CRTCs’ ISMs** are idle.

So the static display’s ISM reaches `OPTIMIZED_IDLE` and turns global idle on, while the cursor display is busy. Xorg’s legacy cursor moves hold no vblank reference, so nothing vetoes it.

issues.description:
## Summary

Two problems, the first one being the main subject of this issue:

1. FRL link training never reaches rate 5 (4×10G) on this sink, because of an FLT_UPDATE timeout.
2. As a consequence, 4K120 needs DSC, and FRL+DSC flickers (likely #5934).

With native HDMI FRL enabled (`amdgpu.dcfeaturemask=0x402`), FRL link-cap verification against a Samsung 2020 TV (QE55Q82T) **always** fails at FRL rate 5 (4 lanes × 10 Gbps). The failure is the same every time: the sink acknowledges the rate and requests LTP patterns, then never sets `FLT_UPDATE` again before the \~200 ms FLT timer expires. The driver then falls back to rate 4 (4 × 8 Gbps), which trains successfully within about 50–70 ms.

Because rate 4 is slightly short of the bandwidth needed for CTA 3840x2160@120 RGB 8 bpc, the driver enables DSC for that mode. With DSC over FRL, the picture **flickers and shows intermittent interference** after a while. This looks like a **second, separate problem**: DSC is within the sink's advertised DSC/FRL caps and should be stable even on a rate-4 link (see #5934). This issue is mainly about the training failure. The DSC instability is noted here because the training failure is what makes DSC necessary on this sink. With DSC disabled (`amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x4`), 4K120 falls back to TMDS YCbCr 4:2:0.

After **any** full GPU reset both of these stop working silently, and stay broken until the device suspends/resumes or the machine reboots. From that point on, VRAM freed by one process is handed to the next process with the previous owner's data still in it.

## Rough steps to reproduce

This affects me daily.

1. A misbehaving shader hangs the GPU. Plenty of examples in tests and other issues. I can provide some examples generated by claude if necessary.
2. The kernel's job timeout resets the GPU (MODE1, "VRAM is lost").
3. From that moment, clearing is broken for the whole machine.
4. Anything that allocates VRAM expecting zeros now gets another process's leftovers. I get repeated crashes in kwin and in spectacle, and in games, and they keep recurring until I reboot.
5. Programs that rely on zeroed memory misbehave and trigger a crash or reset again. Which only excerbates the problem (observed crashes in kwin, spectacles and games on steam).

Forcing a sleep/resume somewhat mitigates the issue but may still lead to crashes because once bad memory is in it persist even with per-queue/soft reset.

## Affected versions

| Kernel | DRM | Fresh boot | After one reset |
|--------|-----|------------|-----------------|
| 6.10.14 | 3.57 | zero | **leaks** |
| 6.12.117 (LTS) | 3.61 | zero | **leaks**

issues.author: Natalie Vock
issues.description:
On my system, while setting up hibernation, I did some misconfigurations that made the final write of the hibernation image to disk fail.

amdgpu proceeded to explode when aborting the hibernation in that state, which I eventually traced to this patch: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20250710062313.3226149-6-guoqing.zhang@amd.com/

Ever since that patch, the final `thaw()` call before writing out the hibernation image is a no-op. That's fine only when the system actually powers down completely afterwards, but that is by no means guaranteed. When hibernation fails and the system resumes, no separate PM resume function is ever called because as far as the PM subsystem is aware, the GPU should be up and running.

Once userspace is thawed, it tries to submit to the sleeping GPU, everything obviously times out, so amdgpu tries to reset the GPU, which also fails because nothing responds anymore. Bonus points if userspace then crashes, upon which the kernel tries to clean up process resources and meets the same fate (well, it hangs when waiting for PT cleanup fences, but my kernel panics on hung tasks).

If I understand the patch correctly, it tries to work around buffers being moved from swap back into RAM/VRAM even though the system is about to power off, but nop-ing out the entire resume process seems like a quick-and-dirty hack more than anything. Was the actual issue just moving buffers around too eagerly? If so, why not try fixing that instead?

/cc @agd5f @superm1

### Description

The whole system hard resets (no kernel panic, no log output) when a game starts a heavy 3D load. On the next boot, the kernel reports:

```
x86/amd: Previous system reset reason [0x08000800]: an uncorrected error caused a data fabric sync flood event
```

The journal of the boot that crashed simply stops, with no amdgpu, AER or MCE messages beforehand. The only message near the crash is sometimes `clocksource: Watchdog remote CPU N read timed out`, which looks like a symptom of the fabric stalling.

**Workaround:** forcing the GPU to a fixed power state prevents the crash completely:

```
echo high > /sys/class/drm/card1/device/power_dpm_force_performance_level
```

With `high`, the same games run at Ultra settings with no problem. With `auto` (the default), they crash every time. This points to DPM / power state transitions during a sudden rise in load.

**Narrowed down to GFXCLK.** Locking only the shader clock at its top level, with MCLK, FCLK and SOCCLK left under automatic control, is enough to prevent the crash:

```
echo manual > /sys/class/drm/card1/device/power_dpm_force_performance_level
echo 2 > /sys/class/drm/card1/device/pp_dpm_sclk
```

issues.author: Faruk Aydin
issues.description:
## Summary

`amdgpu_driver_release_kms()` calls `pci_set_drvdata(adev->pdev, NULL)` (drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_kms.c:1608 in v7.1.2). This function is the DRM `.release` callback, so it runs at the _final_ `drm_dev_put()` — which is deferred until the last userspace reference to the DRM device is dropped, not at unbind time.

In a GPU-passthrough workflow (unbind amdgpu -\> bind vfio-pci, standard VFIO practice), any process still holding the dGPU's DRM node open at unbind time (a GPU monitoring daemon such as LACT, a compositor, etc.) delays the final release past the point where vfio-pci has bound the device and stored its own drvdata. When the last DRM fd closes, amdgpu's deferred release then NULLs **vfio-pci's** drvdata.

Every subsequent vfio-pci path that dereferences drvdata crashes:

- `vfio_pci_remove` -\> `vfio_pci_core_unregister_device` -\> `vfio_pci_core_sriov_configure` (on unbind) — observed, oops attached
- `vfio_pci_core_runtime_suspend` (runtime PM) — observed on an earlier boot
- `vfio_pci_core_aer_err_detected` would equally be affected

A secondary effect makes this worse: the oopsed sysfs `unbind` write dies holding the device lock, so any later PCI operation on the device blocks in uninterruptible D-state. When libvirt is the caller (qemu hook), libvirtd deadlocks until reboot.

issues.title: RX 9070 XT (Navi 48): DMCUB firmware loading fails on kernel 7.0, causing display loss
issues.author: Antoni Duran Rosich
issues.description:
## System

* GPU: ASUS Radeon RX 9070 XT (PCI ID 1002:7550, subsystem 1043:061a)
* Motherboard: ASUS ROG CROSSHAIR X870E HERO
* BIOS: 2503
* OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
* Secure Boot: enabled
* Firmware package: linux-firmware-amd-graphics 0ubuntu3.4

## Problem

With kernel 7.0.0-42-generic, the display loses signal after the boot splash screen. The system does not reach a usable graphical desktop.

The same GPU and monitor can display the desktop when booting kernel 6.8.0-147-lowlatency, although the AMDGPU driver also reports an initialization failure on that kernel.

## Relevant kernel log messages

`failed to load ucode DMCUB(0x3F)
psp gfx command LOAD_IP_FW(0x6) failed and response status is (0x11)
Wait for DMUB auto-load failed: 3
*ERROR* dc_dmub_srv_log_diagnostic_data: DMCUB error`

The GPU is detected, its VBIOS is read, VRAM and GTT are initialized, and Display Core reports DCN 4.0.1 before the DMCUB failure.

I also tested booting without the amdgpu module options `runpm=0` and `dc=1`. The display failure persisted.

## Question

Could this be a DMCUB firmware or AMDGPU Display Core initialization regression affecting Navi 48 / RX 9070 XT on kernel 7.0?

I can provide complete kernel logs and additional diagnostic information.

## Brief summary of the problem:
I have an ASUS TUF A14 FA401EA with Ryzen AI Max+ 392 and Radeon 8060 iGPU. When I play a game after the laptop was woken up from s2idle, 5 to 20 minutes of gameplay trigger a system crash that requires a hard reboot. Both internal and external screens go black all of a sudden and sometimes audio is stuck with a high pitch. All USB peripherals get disconnected and if I use the laptop's keyboard I can't get to a virtual terminal with the Ctrl + Alt + F3 shortcut.

Unfortunately no error message appears in the logs. It's as if you unplugged a desktop PC, even the way the screen goes to black is similar. I tried playing games on:
- GNOME (Wine Wayland + Proton GE)
- GNOME (Nested Gamescope + Proton)
- Gamescope from TTY (Proton)
- GNOME with just the external display (Nested Gamescope + Proton)

This doesn't happen if I don't put the laptop to suspend, games play just fine.
